familyFindings.tops: Legacy Tops are recognizable, original and readable, but consistently centered/front-facing flat vector garments with weak fabric volume, material response and three-quarter collectible presentation. Tier progression relies mostly on motif/color complexity rather than richer construction/materials/lighting.
familyFindings.bottoms: Bottoms are item-readable and distinct enough by category, but the family repeats flat frontal vector silhouettes with drawn-on seams, pockets, pleats, patches and sparkle motifs. The actual Store pixels show very little believable fabric thickness, drape, tailoring, hardware or three-quarter collectible depth, and Tier 4-5 items do not make the required premium material/spectacle jump.

items.name: Hoodie
items.reason: Identity is clear and starter-friendly, but card and selected-detail pixels show a flat front-facing garment icon with little believable fabric volume, fold/material response or three-quarter collectible depth. Preserve the simple Hoodie identity while rebuilding it as a dimensional toy-fashion item with stronger form lighting and material cues.

items.name: Zip Hoodie
items.reason: Zip-hoodie identity and pixel motif read, but the garment remains a flat frontal icon. Add dimensional hood/body separation, zipper/hardware depth, fabric folds and three-quarter lighting without overdecorating Tier 1.

items.name: Varsity Tee
items.reason: The tee and varsity/lightning motif are readable, but the presentation is sparse and two-dimensional. Give the shirt convincing body volume, sleeve/collar construction and material shading while keeping a clean starter-tier silhouette.

items.name: Bow Cardigan
items.reason: Bow/cardigan identity is distinct, but knit, button, bow and cuff details read as flat graphic shapes. Rebuild with knit/soft-material depth, layered bow construction and dimensional lighting suitable for Tier 2.

items.name: Crewneck
items.reason: Galaxy emblem is readable, but the sweatshirt has little dimensional construction or material character and feels close to the same front-facing template as adjacent Tops. Preserve the crewneck simplicity while adding garment volume, ribbing/folds and richer galaxy material/light treatment.

items.name: Gamer Jacket
items.reason: Controller/gamer cues are recognizable, but the jacket layering, hardware and textile/tech materials are rendered as flat shapes. Add dimensional collar/panels, seams/hardware and controlled luminous accents while retaining the exact gamer-jacket identity.

items.name: Colorblock Hoodie
items.reason: Colorblocking separates it visually, but Tier 3 still presents as the same flat frontal hoodie family. Add stronger hood/body dimensionality, seams/folds, material variation and three-quarter collectible framing so progression is more than palette/pattern complexity.

items.name: Puffer Vest
items.reason: Vest silhouette is distinct, but the puffer sections do not convincingly read as lofted/quilted material at card scale. Increase cushion volume, panel highlights/shadows, zipper/opening construction and art-theme detail without losing silhouette clarity.

items.name: Art Smock
items.reason: Paint marks/smock identity are present, but construction is flat and apron/smock layering, tools and fabric depth are not premium at Tier 3. Add layered garment form, pocket/tool or paint-material detail and dimensional lighting while preserving the exact Art Smock concept.

items.name: Star Bomber
items.reason: Star/neon bomber cues read, but Tier 4 does not deliver a meaningful jump in material richness or spectacle; it remains another flat jacket card. Rebuild with dimensional bomber volume, ribbed/reflective materials, hardware and restrained neon rim/glow.

items.name: Cloud Jacket
items.reason: Cloud motif and candy palette are readable, but the jacket lacks Tier-4 dimensional construction, plush/material depth and lighting differentiation. Push cloud/plush volume, seams/hardware and candy-luxe material response without obscuring the jacket silhouette.

items.name: Star Coat
items.reason: The long-coat/star concept is recognizable, but the highest tier lacks the luxe construction, dimensional materials, ornament and controlled hero lighting expected of Tier 5. Create a clearly premium coat silhouette with layered lapels/trim, richer material response and spectacular but readable star detail.

items.name: Jeans
items.reason: Jeans are immediately recognizable and starter-friendly, but actual card plus selected detail/try-on pixels show a flat symmetric cutout with line-drawn seams and almost no denim grain, seam thickness, pocket depth, folds or leg volume. Preserve the simple blue-jeans identity while adding dimensional denim, stitched construction and subtle three-quarter form.

items.name: Joggers
items.reason: Galaxy colors and jogger identity read cleanly, but the garment is still a flat straight-on vector with little gathered waistband/cuff construction, fleece/knit response, pocket depth or draped folds. Rebuild as dimensional soft joggers while keeping Tier 1 restrained.

items.name: Cargo Pants
items.reason: Cargo pockets and sunny palette distinguish the item, but the pockets are flat rectangles on flat legs with no flap thickness, hardware, seam construction, crease volume or believable fabric lighting. Preserve the simple starter cargo concept and add layered pocket/fabric depth.

items.name: Pleat Skirt
items.reason: Pleat-skirt silhouette and Aqua Wave palette are readable, but the pleats are mostly drawn lines on a flat trapezoid. Tier 2 needs real layered pleat depth, waistband thickness, hem volume and richer directional material lighting.

items.name: Overalls
items.reason: Bib, straps and art accents establish the overalls identity, but straps, buttons, bib/pocket and legs are still paper-flat geometry. Add buckle/button hardware, overlapping strap/bib construction, denim/canvas texture, folds and three-quarter leg volume.

items.name: Star Leggings
items.reason: Dark luxe palette and star motifs read, but the leggings remain a flat template with sticker-like decorations. Add stretch-fabric contour and sheen, waistband depth, leg curvature and controlled star-luxe material highlights without making Tier 2 overbusy.

items.name: Sport Shorts
items.reason: Short silhouette and neon piping differentiate the item, but waistband, leg openings and athletic material remain flat and icon-like. Tier 3 needs elastic/drawcord construction, mesh/technical fabric, folds and more convincing dimensional rim light.

items.name: Wide-Leg Pants
items.reason: Wide-leg silhouette and candy palette are legible, but the broad pink shape has little drape, waistband/pleat construction, side volume or fabric response. Build convincing hanging folds and dimensional flare while preserving the clean Candy Core identity.

items.name: Patch Jeans
items.reason: Patch treatment makes the concept readable, but patches and stitches sit on another flat jeans silhouette rather than layered fabric. Add denim body volume, pocket/seam depth, physically layered stitched patches and more adventurous three-quarter construction.

items.name: Utility Skirt
items.reason: Cargo pockets and cloud palette make the utility-skirt concept clear, but Tier 4 still reads as a flat trapezoid with printed pockets. Add structured fabric thickness, layered pockets/flaps, hardware, seams, hem depth and premium cloud-material cues.

items.name: Glitter Cargo
items.reason: Pixel/glitter markers are readable, but sparkle is represented as small dots/squares over the same flat cargo form. Tier 4 needs reflective textile response, layered cargo pockets, buckles/hardware, dimensional folds and a meaningful premium-lighting step up.

items.name: Star Trousers
items.reason: Dark tailored shape, gold waist and star motifs identify the highest-tier trousers, but the actual card remains a flat straight-on silhouette and the star appliques do not create Tier-5 richness. Rebuild with tailored folds and leg volume, metallic trim/hardware, layered star embroidery/gems and controlled hero lighting.
